metaDescription: Six Aprilaire whole-house dehumidifiers compared by pint rating, drain setup and Wi-Fi control, so you can size the right one for a basement or crawl space.
expertTake: The E080 Pro is the pick for most damp basements because its capacity matches a typical 2,000 to 3,000 square foot problem without the larger frame of the 100-pint unit. The E050 is the value pick when the space is modest and you want the same build quality. Anyone with a single small damp room should skip this brand and buy a portable bucket unit instead.
introParagraphs: A whole-house dehumidifier is a different animal from the bucket unit you wheel around a basement. It sits in a corner or hangs in a crawl space, drains on its own, and runs for months without anyone touching it. That changes what matters when you shop.

The decisions that count are capacity for the real moisture load, how the water leaves the machine, and whether the control is something you will actually use. This guide works through one brand's range so the differences between sizes and bundles are easy to see.

products.name: AprilAire E080 Pro 80-Pint Whole-House Dehumidifier
products.description:
The E080 Pro is a compressor machine built around a sealed refrigeration loop, an evaporator coil and a dedicated fan, and it is sized for the kind of moisture load that fills a whole basement rather than one room. It senses room humidity against your target and starts itself, so there is no bucket to empty and no timer to program. The cabinet is built for permanent placement, which is why it feels closer to an appliance than a portable unit.

Its 80-pint rating sits in the middle of the range, one step above the 70-pint E070 and one step below the 100-pint E100. That middle position is why it suits most homes: a finished or semi-finished basement that regularly climbs above 60 percent relative humidity in summer usually needs this much coil area. If your space is a sealed crawl space, the smaller E070 is the better fit because of its frame, and if the home is large and leaky the E100 gives more headroom.

Ownership is simple. You wash the filter on a schedule, vacuum the coil once a year, and keep the drain line clear. Because the unit is meant to run for long stretches, a gravity drain to a floor drain or sump is the cleanest arrangement, and a condensate pump is the fallback when the floor slopes the wrong way.
products.bestFor: Damp basements in mid-size homes that need a set-and-forget machine.
pros: Capacity suits most full basements without oversizing
Smart sensing starts and stops on its own
Energy Star Most Efficient rating keeps running cost down
Built for permanent placement with a continuous drain
cons: Needs a drain path, so it is poor for a bucket-only setup
Large and heavy compared with portable units
Overkill for one small damp room

products.name: AprilAire E100 Pro 100-Pint Whole-House Dehumidifier
products.description:
The E100 Pro uses the same cabinet philosophy as the E080 but moves more air across a larger coil to reach 100 pints per day. At the top of the Pro range it is built for homes where moisture arrives from several directions at once: a big open basement, a slab with a high water table, or a house with a leaky crawl space connected to the living area.

The extra 20 pints over the E080 matters most when the humidity problem is chronic rather than seasonal. A machine running close to its rated capacity runs nearly all day and wears faster, while one with spare capacity cycles on and off and lasts longer. That is the real argument for buying up a size, more than the headline number.

Expect the same upkeep as the smaller units, with a bigger drain flow to plan for. At full output it can pour out about 12 gallons a day, so a pump or a good gravity run is essential, and a bucket is not an option. If you only need to hold a 1,600 square foot space, the E050 does it for less outlay and less floor area.
products.bestFor: Large or leaky homes where moisture load stays high all year.

products.name: AprilAire E070 Pro 70-Pint Crawl Space Dehumidifier

specList.label: Best space
specList.value: Sealed crawl space or tight basement

products.description:
What sets the E070 Pro apart is its shape. At 12.5 by 12.5 by 25 inches it fits through most crawl space access doors and between joists, which is where the larger units simply cannot go. Homes up to 2,200 square feet are within its listed rating, and it comes with a drain hose, so a crawl space install does not need extra parts on day one.

Its 70-pint capacity is a step below the E080, so in a wide-open basement it will run longer than the bigger models. In a sealed crawl space with a vapor barrier the load is much lower and the small frame is the whole point. Compared with the E050 it gives 20 more pints and a hose in the box, which is why it earns the crawl space badge.

Crawl spaces are hard on equipment, so plan around that. Mount it off the dirt on a platform or hang it, run the drain to a sump or discharge outdoors, and leave a clear path to the filter for yearly service. A unit tucked into a tight space you never visit is the one that quietly fails, so schedule the visit.
products.bestFor: Sealed crawl spaces and tight mechanical areas where size decides.

Drain hose included for a simple first install
Rated for homes up to 2,200 square feet
Sized sensibly for a vapor-barriered crawl space
cons: Runs longer than the E080 in a big basement
Service access in a crawl space is awkward
Needs a platform or hanger to stay off damp ground

products.name: AprilAire E050PZ 50-Pint Whole-House Dehumidifier
products.description:
The E050PZ is the entry point to the range and the lightest unit in it at 46 pounds, with built-in handles that make it easy to carry down basement stairs. Coverage is listed at up to 1,600 square feet, and a Wi-Fi capable control gives remote adjustment without a separate purchase decision.

The trade is capacity. At 50 pints it has less than two thirds of the E080 rating of 80 pints, so it suits a mild or moderate problem: a finished basement that gets muggy in July, or a tight, well-sealed space. In a wet unfinished basement it will run flat out and still lag.

Because it is lighter and lower in profile, it is the friendliest model for anyone who wants to move the machine for cleaning or relocate it between seasons. Treat it as the sensible choice when the space is under about 1,600 square feet and spend the saved outlay on a decent pump or a hygrometer.
products.bestFor: Smaller basements and homes under 1,600 square feet with a moderate problem.
pros: Lightest model at 46 pounds with carry handles
Wi-Fi capable control included in the listing
Right-sized for spaces up to 1,600 square feet
Same build quality as the larger Pro units
cons: Runs near its limit in a wet unfinished basement
Smaller capacity leaves little headroom in humid summers

products.name: AprilAire E080W Smart Wi-Fi 80-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump
products.description:
This is the E080 platform with two changes that matter: built-in Wi-Fi with the AprilAire Connect app, and a low-profile condensate pump with bracket and tubing in the bundle. Capacity stays at 80 pints per day, so the coil and fan behave the same as the E080 Pro described above.

The pump is the real draw. Many basements have no floor drain near the machine, and the bundle lifts water up and away to a laundry sink or an outdoor discharge. Buying the pump separately for the wired E080 gets you to a similar place, but the bundle removes the compatibility question.

The app lets you change the target humidity and watch conditions from another room, which is useful in a vacation home or a rental where you want to confirm it is running. Keep the local humidistat in mind as the fallback: a machine that depends on a cloud service for basic control is a worse appliance, so confirm the unit still holds its setpoint with the Wi-Fi off.
products.bestFor: Basements without a floor drain where remote monitoring is a plus.
pros: Condensate pump and tubing come in the bundle
App control for humidity target and status
Same 80-pint capacity as the E080 Pro
Removes the pump compatibility guesswork
cons: Costs more than the plain E080 Pro for features some skip
Pump adds a small component that can eventually need service

products.name: AprilAire E100W Smart Wi-Fi 100-Pint Dehumidifier
products.description:
The E100W takes the 100-pint chassis and adds Wi-Fi control. It is aimed at buyers with the biggest moisture problems who also want to keep an eye on the machine remotely, such as owners of second homes or large finished basements that cannot be allowed to climb in humidity.

Compared with the wired E100 Pro the practical difference is connectivity, not coil performance. Both pull up to 100 pints a day, so the decision comes down to whether the app is worth the added cost to you. In a home you visit daily, the plain Pro is the better dollar; in a lake house left empty for weeks, remote visibility earns its keep.

Plan the drain before you buy. At this output there is no sensible alternative to a gravity run or a pump, and the volume is high enough that a kinked line will flood a floor in hours rather than days. Test the drain with a bucket of water on day one.
products.bestFor: Large second homes and big basements where remote checks matter.
pros: Top 100-pint capacity with remote control
Commercial-grade, USA-assembled construction
Energy Star certified for lower running cost
Useful for homes left empty for weeks
cons: Needs a robust drain plan at full output
Wi-Fi is only worth it if you will actually check it

buyingCriteria.explanation: Pint ratings describe how much water the machine can pull in a day under a stated test, so they only help if you compare like with like. The E050PZ at 50 pints suits about 1,600 square feet, while the E080 Pro at 80 pints and the E100 Pro at 100 pints are built for larger or wetter spaces. A common mistake is sizing by floor area alone, when a basement with a high water table can need a unit one size up from what its square footage suggests.

A whole-house unit has no practical bucket, so the water path decides whether the install works. The E070 Pro ships with a drain hose for gravity flow, and the E080W comes with a condensate pump and tubing for spaces without a floor drain. Buyers often discover too late that a floor drain sits uphill of the machine, which is the situation a pump bundle solves.

The E070 Pro measures 12.5 by 12.5 by 25 inches, which is the reason it passes through crawl space doors that the larger Pro units cannot. The E050PZ weighs 46 pounds and has built-in handles, so it can be carried down stairs by one person. Measure the narrowest door or hatch on the route before choosing the model, because a unit that cannot reach its spot is a return.

Wired Pro models use a humidistat with smart sensing, while the E080W and E100W add Wi-Fi and the AprilAire Connect app. Remote control helps in a second home, but the setpoint should hold locally if the network drops. Verify that a Wi-Fi-less install still runs normally before you rely on the app.

A machine that runs for months pays its electricity bill many times over, so efficiency matters more than for an occasional-use portable. The E080 Pro and E100 Pro carry the Energy Star Most Efficient designation, which means less energy per pint removed. Between two similar-capacity options, favor the certified one and the one with spare headroom so it cycles rather than runs flat out.

The listings separate basement, crawl space and whole-house use, and the labels reflect real differences. A sealed crawl space has a smaller load but a tight entry, which favors the E070 Pro. A large open basement favors the E080 Pro or E100 Pro, and a modest finished one favors the E050PZ. Choosing for the actual space beats choosing for the largest number.

specDecoder.meaning: The amount of water the machine can remove in 24 hours at a stated temperature and humidity. A higher number means a bigger coil and fan, not automatically a better fit.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare the 50, 70, 80 and 100 pint ratings in this lineup against the test condition each listing states.

specDecoder.meaning: A designation for units that remove more water per kilowatt hour than the standard Energy Star level. It lowers running cost on a machine that runs for months.
specDecoder.watchFor: The E080 Pro and E100 Pro carry it, so check the badge before assuming a bundle shares it.

specDecoder.meaning: A small pump that lifts collected water through tubing to a distant drain. It solves the case where the floor drain is uphill or across the room.
specDecoder.watchFor: The E080W includes one, while the E100 Pro and E080 Pro rely on a gravity drain unless you add a pump.

specDecoder.meaning: The unit reads room humidity and starts and stops itself against a setpoint. This replaces timers and manual switching.
specDecoder.watchFor: Confirm the E050PZ and Wi-Fi models still hold the setpoint on the local control.

specDecoder.meaning: The width, depth and height of the cabinet, which decides whether it fits through a hatch or between joists. It also affects how easily the unit can be serviced.
specDecoder.watchFor: The E070 Pro at 12.5 by 12.5 by 25 inches is the compact option in this lineup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity versus space
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared each unit's pint rating with the space it is listed for, from the 50-pint E050PZ at 1,600 square feet to the 100-pint E100W. We looked for models whose rating is not stretched beyond what the coil can plausibly do. Rated capacity is a spec sheet figure, not a measurement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drain flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each model removes water: gravity hose, included pump or optional pump. A unit that fits more floor plans scores higher. The E080W with pump and the E070 Pro with hose were the easiest to plan around.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed cabinet design, handles, weight and filter access based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns. The 46 pound E050PZ is the easiest to move, while the crawl space unit prioritizes size. Easy filter access scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and connectivity
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated humidistat control from the app-connected models and judged whether the app adds real value. Remote status is helpful for second homes. Local control that works without the cloud is a requirement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Efficiency and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed Energy Star status and capacity against the relative price tier. The E050PZ and E070 Pro sit lowest, the bundles in the middle and the E100W at the top. Value here means fit, not the lowest number.

cards.label: Wired Pro (E080 Pro, E100 Pro)
cards.text: These use a local humidistat with smart sensing and no app. They cost less, have fewer failure points and suit homes you visit daily. The E080 Pro is the typical choice and the E100 Pro adds capacity.

cards.label: Smart Wi-Fi (E080W, E100W)
cards.text: These add the AprilAire Connect app for remote setpoint and status, and the E080W includes a pump. They suit second homes and owners who want to confirm the unit is running while away.

howToChoose.note: Choose wired for a primary home you check often, and smart for a second home or a rental.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Capacity at or above the moisture load, a drain route that works with gravity or a pump, and a cabinet you can carry downstairs. Place it with clearance around the intake and keep it off a wet floor.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The E080 Pro is the default basement pick. The E050PZ suits a small finished basement, and the E080W is the choice when the drain is far away.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The home is large or leaky, you are away for weeks, or running time is nearly constant. The E100 Pro and E100W give headroom, and the Wi-Fi models give remote visibility.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The space is under 1,600 square feet or tightly sealed. The E050PZ or E070 Pro cover it, and a separate hygrometer is a cheaper way to confirm results.

maintenance.why: A clogged filter chokes airflow and makes the coil freeze. Rinse it and let it dry fully before reinstalling.
Dust on the evaporator coil cuts efficiency and adds to running time. Power the unit off and unplug it first.
Slime and kinks stop flow and can back water into the cabinet. Pour a cup of water through to confirm it runs.
A condensate pump that sticks leads to overflow. Lift the float and listen for it to run.

maintenance.task: Verify humidity with a separate hygrometer
maintenance.why: A built-in humidistat can drift a few points. A cheap hygrometer confirms the real reading.

faq.q: Which Aprilaire size do I need?
faq.a: Start from the space and the severity of the problem. The E050PZ covers about 1,600 square feet at moderate humidity, the E080 Pro suits most full basements, and the E100 Pro is for large or chronically wet homes. If you are between sizes, choose the larger one so it cycles instead of running constantly.

faq.q: Is a smart Wi-Fi model worth the extra cost?
faq.a: It is worth it for a second home, a rental or any space you cannot check often. In a home you visit daily, the wired Pro models do the same dehumidifying work for less.

faq.q: How long will one of these last?
faq.a: Compressor machines commonly last 5 to 10 years, and a commercial-grade cabinet with a good filter routine sits at the upper end. Cleaning the filter and coil is the main lever. Units run flat out in an undersized setup wear faster.

faq.q: Does a higher pint number mean it works better?
faq.a: Not by itself. The rating depends on the test temperature and humidity, and a larger unit only helps if the space has the moisture to justify it. An oversized unit in a dry space still just cycles off.

faq.q: Can I use one without a drain?
faq.a: Not practically. These are whole-house units meant to drain continuously, and at 80 to 100 pints a day a bucket would overflow in hours. Use the E080W with its pump, or plan a gravity run.
Slightly. Compressor heat enters the space, so expect the area to warm by a few degrees. In a cold basement that is often welcome, and in a crawl space it is a non-issue.
